doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The 1960s groups, Madison Avenue and film
title: Why he likes trombones
summary: He likes the trombone because it is closest to the human voice, names Garnett Brown and others, and mentions a four-trombone band with Jimmy Cheatham.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Well again, you know, one of the interesting features of your band is that you like trombone players. You bring in Garnett Brown.
Well the bone, I’ll tell you, the bone -- you know why? Trombones are about the closest instrument to the human voice that there is. I didn’t know whether you knew that

or not, did you, or realize that, but a trombone is very close to a human voice, especially when its played by people like, you know, Garnett, George Mahana and all these hell of a trombone players, JJ and people like that. You know, trombone is a hell of a sound. I just -- you know, I like the sound of a trombone. I like the sound of the combination of a trombone and horn. I like the trombone with a flute. I like trombone with tenor. I like trombone, you know, with alto. I like the trombone.
As a matter of fact man, I had a trombone band at one time. I’ve got the record here, man. I had four bones, and a singer, and a horn player, alto player, and a bass player. That was it.
Who wrote for that? Who arranged for that?
Oh, Cheatham, Jimmy Cheatham, there you go.
Yeah, I got a record over here. But anyway, it’s cool. You dig?
